overall_summary: The channel heavily focuses on 'self respect' and smartphone-related micro-interactions (chats, names, blocks). While view counts are generally low (single digits to low 40s), themes around decisive self-respect actions (deleting chats, ending wait times) slightly outperform generic overthinking or deep night thoughts. However, due to low overall sample size and zero engagement (likes/comments), confidence remains low and controlled experimentation is required.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'rwOUYo_hayQ' (41 views) and 'AfaLxMy6FMY' (41 views) perform better than average when tied to specific digital cleanup moments like status lists or chat deletions.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing short-form narratives around tactile smartphone UI actions representing emotional detachment.

weak_patterns.pattern: Vague or abstract emotional hooks without a concrete anchor
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'hT4EGP69mRw' (3 views) and 'c7epDdpUJis' (5 views) featuring softer or more generalized setups underperformed significantly.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract emotional statements and anchor every hook in an immediate, recognizable physical action.

next_video.reason: Previous mid-day and early afternoon uploads (e.g., around 13:40 UTC/IST slots) captured some of the higher view counts in the dataset. Testing a fresh UI element (Share Sheet) keeps the winning digital cleanup theme alive without repeating exact phrases.

experiment: Testing a new digital touchpoint (Share Sheet shortcut) to see if smartphone UI-based self-respect hooks continue to hold relative attention over standard chat deletions.
